title: Dating overwhelm — Nadia, 36, and the 48-hour no
caption:
Not knowing hurts more than a no. Stress peaks at 50/50 odds, not at bad news (Nature Comms, 2016).
Give it 48 hours, then call it. Send this to her.
How many apps are you on?
www.aiforheratx.org
#datingapps #ghosting #womensmentalhealth #datingfatigue #womenshealth #anxiety

scenes.text: He didn't say no. He said *nothing*. Not knowing wrecks you more than a no.

scenes.text: Nadia is 36, divorced two years, and she's read his last message nine times.
phrases: Nadia's 36. Divorced two years, back on the apps since March.
She's read his last message nine times. It says 'haha yeah'.
By 1 a.m. she's editing herself: too keen, too dull, too much?
She's not sad about him. She's worn out from guessing.

scenes.text: Being ignored runs on the brain's pain circuitry (Science, 2003). She isn't being dramatic.
phrases: Maybe don't text first next time
I don't want him. I want to stop refreshing.

scenes.text: Tonight: no reply in 48 hours counts as a no. Archive the chat and go to bed.
phrases: 48 hours, no reply? Call it a no and archive the chat.
Keep 3 conversations, max — more options make us choose worse (Psych Science, 2010).
Then take a 20-minute walk tomorrow; WHO says 150 minutes a week.
